_meta.what: Number of DISTINCT "Vagón N" numbers printed on each official station plano.
_meta.why: The catalog keys wagons A/B/C but signage reads Vagón 1/2/3. The letter->number mapping is only safe when the catalog wagon count equals the printed plate count; where they differ the catalog groups platforms differently from the signage (Calle 161: catalog 2 vs printed 4; Av. Jiménez: catalog 5 vs printed 3). See spec 5.5.4.
_meta.source: Counted from the plano images published at tramites.transmilenio.gov.co/station-maps/api/map. Only this count is stored - no image is copied or redistributed.
_meta.regenerate: Re-run the plate counter over a fresh download of the planos; see spec 5.5.4.
_meta.distinct_not_occurrences: Count distinct numbers, not plate images. An island platform is drawn as two rows with its OWN number repeated above and below: Terminal (TM0031) prints "Vagón 1" twice for one vagón. Counting occurrences gave 2, which matched the catalog's 2 wagons, so the gate trusted the mapping and published a "Vagón 2" that exists nowhere in the station — the exact wrong answer this dataset exists to prevent. Verified against the published plano 2026-08-11.
_meta.occurrences_bug_survived: …and the 2026-08-11 recount did NOT catch every case. Av. Chile (TM0061) was stored as 6 against three lettered wagons; its plano draws the two carriageways as two rows, each labelled Vagón 3 / Vagón 2 / Vagón 1 — six rectangles, THREE distinct numbers. Corrected to 3, and the sheet confirms the mapping member for member: Vagón 1 is wagon A (4, B72, H72), Vagón 2 is B (B16, C25, K16, L25), Vagón 3 is C (D22, E32, F32, G22). The signature is mechanical — a stored count exactly DOUBLE the catalog's lettered wagons — and nine stations still carry it, unverified: TM0139 Bicentenario (6=2x3), TM0131 El Tiempo (4=2x2), TM0129 CAN - British Council (4=2x2), TM0060 NQS Calle 75 (4=2x2), TM0148 Tygua-San José (4=2x2), TM0057 Quirigua (2=2x1), TM0051 Ferias (2=2x1), TM0116 Biblioteca (2=2x1), TM0117 Parque (2=2x1). A signature is a lead, not a reading: each still needs its own sheet opened before its count is changed, because a station CAN genuinely have twice the platforms the catalog groups.
_meta.a_drawn_box_is_not_a_vagon: TM0121 Las Aguas was the tenth station carrying that doubled signature and it is corrected to 1 — but NOT because the second box repeats a number. Its plano ('versión noviembre de 2025') draws two rectangles in platform styling, both labelled 'Vagón 1', and the lower one is not a platform at all: no bus calls there, it has no doors and no exit, because it is the mouth of the Las Aguas–Universidades pedestrian tunnel. That fact is not recoverable from the image. Counting distinct numbers happens to give the right answer here (1, matching the catalog's single lettered wagon), but it would have given 2 had the operator numbered the tunnel differently, and no rule about counting shapes or numbers can tell a platform from a corridor drawn like one. This is the reason the file says 'counted', maintained by hand: the plate count is a reading of a drawing by someone who knows the station, and an automated pass over these images cannot be trusted to produce it.
_meta.audit_2026_08_28: Sheets read by hand against the stored counts. Of the first eight, seven disagreed and one (TM0018 Calle 100, see verified_correct) was already right — so a stored count is unreliable, not uniformly wrong. TM0046 Polo 4->3, TM0103 San Mateo 2->3, TM0028 Toberín 4->5, TM0061 Av. Chile 6->3, TM0121 Las Aguas 2->1, TM0137 Las Nieves 3->2. In every one of the six the plano's count equalled the CATALOG's lettered-wagon count, and in every one the services on each numbered vagón matched that letter's members — mostly exactly, never contradicting. The catalog was right each time and the automated pass was wrong each time. Do NOT conclude from this that the counts can simply be set equal to the lettered-wagon count: that would make the gate always pass, and the gate exists precisely for the stations where the two genuinely differ — Terminal (island platform, one number for two catalog wagons), Av. Jiménez and Ricaurte (verified splits, where one code covers two physical stations). Those are real and would then publish wrong vagón numbers. The conclusion is narrower and more annoying: 41 stations are still silent on a mismatch, most are probably miscounts, and each has to be read.
_meta.tz022_added: 2026-08-25. The three Avenida Ciudad de Cali stations (TM90009 Tibanica - Primavera, TM90010 Los Laureles, TM90011 Islandia) had no published plano when this dataset was first counted. They do now — sheets dated 'versión agosto de 2026', legend carrying Z Troncal Avenida Ciudad de Cali — and all three print TWO vagones.
_meta.arcgis_disagrees: ArcGIS consulta_estaciones_troncales files vagones=4 for TM90010 and TM90011 (2 for TM90009); the planos print 2 at all three. The plano wins: it is the sign the rider reads, and it is the artifact this dataset is defined against. troncal_stations.json still records the ArcGIS number verbatim, because that file is the register as published and is regenerated by sync:stations.
_meta.layouts_what: The station's shape, for stations whose shape the catalog cannot express. Rows of printed vagones in the order the sheet draws them, each vagon naming the services on its two long edges (arriba / abajo) — PER VAGON, not per platform, because a vagon can serve one direction while its neighbour serves both (Calle 85: vagon 4 southbound only, vagon 3 northbound only, vagones 2 and 1 both). A row carries offset, how far along the drawing it starts in vagon columns: the stagger between two platforms that do not line up (La Castellana). destinos (codigo -> destination) picks which variant boards a vagon where the catalog files that codigo twice there.
_meta.layouts_why: The drawn plan assumes one segmented platform with both directions along it, which is what most stations are. A staggered station is not: two platforms sit on opposite carriageways, offset from each other, with the busway between. La Castellana (TM0059) is the case that forced this. Its plano prints four vagones across two offset platforms, the catalog files two wagons, and each catalog wagon straddles BOTH platforms — A holds B28 (upper) and G12 (lower), B holds B12/B72 (upper) and F28/H72 (lower). Worse, the stored plate count was 2, which MATCHED the two lettered wagons, so the numbering gate passed and the page published 'Vagón 1: B28 y G12' — two services on opposite sides of a road, named as one platform. That is the failure the gate exists to prevent, reached by a wrong count rather than by a right one. A layout says nothing the sheet does not; where a station has none, the lettered bar is drawn as before. Calle 85 (TM0016) is the second case and a different shape: one straight platform of four vagones where the catalog files three wagons, its C merging printed vagones 3 and 4. Its stored count was 3, matching those three wagons, so the gate passed and C published as "Vagon 3" — sending anyone boarding C50, D10 or H27 to a platform they do not board. Same failure as La Castellana, reached the same way: a wrong plate count that happened to agree with the catalog.
_meta.layouts_gate: A layout is checked against the catalog before it is drawn: every código in it must be a service the catalog files at that station, and every troncal service the catalog files must appear in it. A sheet that has drifted from the network is a stale drawing, and a stale drawing of a platform is exactly what this file exists to prevent — so on any mismatch the layout is dropped and the station falls back to the lettered bar.
_meta.wagons_what: Which lettered vagón a service boards from, for the (station, código) pairs the catalog files under wagon "0" — the pool it uses when upstream sends no `vagon` on the recorrido stop. Read off the same plano as the counts.
_meta.wagons_why: A service in "0" takes no vagón number on any surface, so the station page lists it with no platform at all. The plano prints the platform, so the answer exists; leaving it blank is a gap, and guessing it from the other services' letters would be an invention. Applied at the sync edge (`plateWagon`, tm_api) so the catalog on disk carries it, and re-applied by `npm run prune` to a catalog already written. If upstream ever fills the field in and disagrees with the sheet, the sync says so rather than silently preferring one.
_meta.wagon_zero_is_not_all_gap: Wagon "0" holds two different things and only a plano tells them apart. A PADRON or TRONCAL service there is usually a real gap — it boards a vagón and the recorrido just did not say which (that is what `wagons` below fixes). An ALIMENTADOR or URBANO service there is usually CORRECT: it boards from the street or the integration zone and has no vagón to name. San Mateo's plano is the proof — CSM (Circular San Mateo, ALIMENTADOR) is drawn at 'Integración con servicio urbano', outside the platforms, so its place in "0" is the right answer and nothing should move it. Of the 109 services in "0" at stations with lettered wagons, 68 are PADRON or TRONCAL and 41 are ALIMENTADOR or URBANO; do not read the whole pool as a defect.
_meta.plano_content_vs_catalog: A plano lists services as well as vagones, and the two sources do not always agree on WHICH services. Toberín's sheet ('versión agosto de 2026') prints S46 on Vagón 1 — a Troncal Soacha código the catalog does not carry at all — and prints no G46 anywhere, while the catalog files G46 at two wagons on the strength of its own recorrido. Nothing is changed here on that basis: which routes serve a station is answered by the recorrido (spec 5.1.2), and this file only ever answers how many vagones there are and which one a service boards from. Recorded because the next reader of this sheet will notice the same thing.
_meta.counts_can_be_wrong: TM0028 Toberín was stored as 4 and its plano prints 5, matching the catalog's five lettered wagons exactly — Vagón 5 holds E (H72), Vagón 4 holds D (8, J70, J74) and Vagón 3 holds C (B16, B46, B74, B75, G11, H27, H75), member for member. TM0103 San Mateo was stored as 2 and its plano prints 3 ('versión mayo de 2026'), which cost the busiest station in this audit (62k riders a day) its vagón numbers. Its three vagones hold the catalog's C, B and A: K43+B46 on Vagón 3, E42 on Vagón 2, E48+G45+L41 on Vagón 1. Likewise TM0046 Polo - FINCOMERCIO was stored as 4 and its published plano prints 3 (Vagón 1/2/3, 'versión agosto de 2026'). The count came from the 2026-08-11 automated pass, so that pass has at least one error beyond the occurrences-vs-distinct bug below, and a stored count is not self-verifying. The correction is checkable and was checked: with the four services this file now places out of wagon "0", the plano's three vagones hold exactly the catalog's C, B and A — 6/6, 4/4 and 6/6 members. Any station where the plate count disagrees with the catalog's lettered-wagon count deserves the same look before it is believed to be a genuine grouping difference; that disagreement is what withholds the numbering, so a miscount silently costs a station its vagón numbers.
_meta.tm0002_source: TM0002 Calle 72 - Areandina is counted from a DIFFERENT artifact, and the difference is recorded rather than hidden: its plano has not been published since the station reopened on 2026-08-25. The count of 3 comes from TRANSMILENIO's own closure notice for Calle 76 ('Cierre definitivo estación Calle 76 debido a las obras de construcción del Metro de Bogotá', 2026-08), which lists Calle 72's services under headed blocks Vagón 1 / Vagón 2 / Vagón 3. It is the operator publishing the same numbering for the same station, so it counts; replace it with the plano when one appears. The letter->number mapping is not assumed here either — the notice's Vagón 1 block holds exactly the catalog's wagon A (B18, B23, B75, 6, 8, K23) and its Vagón 3 exactly wagon C (6, 8, D24, F60, J24, L18), member for member. Only Vagón 2 differs, by carrying G52 (see recorrido_corrections.json).
_meta.layouts_destinos: A plate prints ONE chip per código; the catalog can carry several variants of that código boarding the same platform. La Castellana Vagón 1 is the case: the catalog files G12 twice southbound, to P. Sur and to G. Santander, and the sheet prints a single G12. Two chips there claim two boardable services where a rider sees one sign. Which variant it is, is a question about the network and is answered here (`destinos`: código -> the destination whose variant boards this vagón), never inferred — picking one by order would be a coin toss printed as a fact. A código with no entry keeps every variant the direction filter allows.
_meta.verified_correct: Sheets read by hand and found ALREADY correct — recorded so they are not read twice, and because they are the counterweight to the corrections above. TM0018 Calle 100 - Marketmedios (2026-08-28, plano version junio de 2025): three vagones, plates 3 = 3 lettered wagons, and the mapping confirmed member for member — Vagon 3 is wagon C (8, B26, B27, D10, F26), Vagon 2 is B (8, B10, B75, G46, H75), Vagon 1 is A (B12, B46, G12, H27). An ordinary straight platform, both directions along it, which the drawn bar already describes: no layout needed. It is also the highest-traffic station in this audit at 77k riders a day, so its being right matters as much as the seven that were wrong. TM0031 Terminal (2026-09-01, plano version noviembre de 2025): confirmed as the island platform this file already documents — ONE Vagon 1, drawn once per carriageway either side of the concourse, with the Retorno loop at the end. Stored count 1 is right and the numbering stays withheld against the catalog two wagons, which is the correct outcome. No layout either: the catalog A/B are not the sheet two faces. The upper face reads B11 B16 B18 8 and the lower 8 G11 K16 L18, while the catalog files B18 in B beside K16 and L18 and everything else on that face in A, so it does not decompose; the sheet is also ten months old and predates D55 and B55. It stays on the scanner flagged list as prints=1 against wagons=2, which is the signature of this shape rather than a fault. TM0093 General Santander (2026-09-01): resolved by deck geometry rather than by a plate count, because the plate count is what misled at Boyaca. Its sheet draws THREE deck columns side by side at x=307, 519 and 850, each about 145px wide — the same spacing as Calle 100 three — while labelling only two of them; the pair of slabs at x=307 is one platform split by a turnstile row, not two. Stored 3, catalog wagons 3, decks 3: everything agrees and the station already publishes A=1, B=2, C=3. The scanner reported printed=2 and that was the unlabelled-plate undercount, not a fault in the station. Its four wagon-0 entries (12-1, G543, H604, H632) are zonal and correctly platform-less. TM0054 Granja - Carrera 77 and TM0111 Calle 40 Sur (2026-09-01): both already correct — Granja four vagones against stored 4 and four wagons, Calle 40 Sur three against stored 3 and three wagons. Both were flagged only because the deck detector counted their ZONAL ARRIVAL BAYS as platforms: Granja 5-1 Suba-Rincon and 5-3 Serena Cerezos strip above and 5-4 Florida below, Calle 40 Sur Llegada de Pasajeros block. Those are drawn in the same pale grey as a platform but sit well outside the platform band, so the detector now keeps only decks whose vertical span reaches the plates.
_meta.tm0132_no_layout: AV. Rojas - UNISALESIANA prints SIX vagones (3/2/1 on the Calle 26 platform, 6/5/4 on the AutoNorte one) against three catalog wagons, so its count is corrected to 6 and its numbering is now correctly withheld — before this it published A/B/C as Vagon 1/2/3 while A actually merges printed Vagon 1 (K16, K23) with Vagon 4 (B16, B23), sending half its riders across the busway. A LAYOUT IS NOW FILED (2026-09-01). It was withheld because the sheet predates G53 and K53 and the gate would have dropped them from the page; the gate no longer rejects a sheet for missing a service, and unplaced services are listed under the drawing instead. K86 and M86 stay in wagon 0 for the same reason: the sheet places them on Vagon 3 and Vagon 6, but the wagons map keys on catalog LETTERS and no letter corresponds to either of those platforms alone. Re-file both when a current sheet is published.
_meta.tm0027_no_layout: Calle 161 prints FOUR vagones (stored 3, catalog 2 wagons) in the same bridge-split shape as Calle 106 and Calle 142, so the count is corrected to 4 and its numbering is correctly withheld. No layout is filed because the sheet and the catalog disagree about ONE service and no mapping reconciles them: the sheet puts B50 above Vagon 2, while the catalog files B50 in wagon A beside D55 and H13 (Vagon 3) and B28 and B55 (Vagon 1). Read as A = Vagon 3 + Vagon 1 every other member lines up and B50 is the lone exception; read as A = the northbound half, B13 goes missing instead. The sheet is version noviembre de 2024 and the catalog is three days old, so the likelier answer is that B50 moved — but which platform a service boards is exactly what must not be guessed. Fix the count now, file the layout when a current sheet settles B50.
_meta.a_sheet_can_omit_a_label: TM0052 Boyaca was recorded as an island like Terminal on 2026-09-01 and that was WRONG — corrected the same day when the maintainer, who has been to the station, said it has two vagones. It does. Its sheet prints one Vagon 1 plate, but it draws TWO platform decks 257px wide side by side at x=428 and x=690, the same arrangement as Calle 100 three 147px decks; the left one simply carries no label. Terminal is the genuine island and its geometry says so differently: two decks 365px wide at the SAME x, stacked at y=237 and y=387, which is one platform seen from both carriageways. So counting printed plates UNDERCOUNTS wherever a sheet omits a label, and prints=1 against two lettered wagons is not by itself the island signature. Deck geometry separates the two: decks side by side are vagones, decks stacked are faces. Boyaca corrected to 2, which also makes its lettering publish correctly — A is the right deck (6, D20, H20) and prints as Vagon 1, B the left (B10, D10, D22, G22) as Vagon 2.
_meta.tm0146_no_layout: Museo Nacional prints TWO vagones and stored 2 is already right. No layout is filed because its sheet (version noviembre de 2025) predates M47, M51 and M85, three services the catalog now files there; a layout drawn from it would drop all three from the page. What the sheet CAN settle is the wagon-0 pool: it puts D81, M86 and L81 on Vagon 2 (catalog B) and K86 and P85 on Vagon 1 (catalog A). M85 is not on the sheet and stays unplaced.
_meta.dividers: What separates the two platforms of a split station is answered per station, never inferred from the drawing. This started wrong: every divider was drawn as a busway on no evidence at all. El Tiempo (TM0131), AV. Rojas (TM0132) and Tygua - San Jose (TM0148) are split by a CICLORRUTA, and Guatoque - Veraguas (TM0147) by a CANO, an open water channel. The sheets do encode it — the ciclorruta ones draw bici glyphs on the dividing line and Guatoque draws it in blue — but it was read past. Corrected on the maintainer word, who knows the stations. AV. Rojas and Tygua have no layout yet, so their answer lives here until one is filed. La Castellana (TM0059), NQS Calle 75 (TM0060) and Av. Chile (TM0061) are split by the RAILWAY that runs down the NQS — answered by the maintainer, who has been to them; the sheets draw it as a plain grey band and nothing on them says it is a rail corridor. A station with no answer on file — La Castellana included, which has never been checked — gets a plain separator that claims nothing.
_meta.counts_scan_2026_09_01: The scanner (scripts/ocr/planos.mjs) re-read all 127 sheets and found 23 stored counts that disagree with the sheet. 16 were applied and 7 were deliberately NOT, and the split is geometric. A sheet draws one bar per vagon at an ordinary station; at a station whose two platforms face each other it draws the SAME vagon once per carriageway, so the bar count doubles. Both look like 'decks=2 vagones=2' to the scanner and it files both under 'ordinary shape, only the stored number is wrong' — which is wrong for the doubled ones, and dangerously so: applying the count would make plates equal wagons and START publishing a vagon number for a split station drawn as a single bar, the exact La Castellana failure this dataset exists to prevent. TM0148 Tygua - San Jose proves it, because the maintainer has already told us it is split by a ciclorruta and the scanner still called it ordinary. HELD, all with doubled bars, all on a corridor that already has a confirmed split station: TM0060 and TM0148 (NQS Central, which has La Castellana and Guatoque), TM0128, TM0129, TM0130 and TM0134 (Calle 26, which has El Tiempo and AV. Rojas and whose ciclorruta runs the length of the corridor between them), and TM0030 Calle 187 (Autonorte, one deck region against two catalog wagons, ambiguous on its own). Each needs its sheet read. APPLIED, all with one bar per vagon and decks, plates and wagons all three agreeing: TM0005, TM0008, TM0011, TM0038, TM0047, TM0056, TM0064, TM0074, TM0075, TM0077, TM0079, TM0081, TM0082, TM0084, TM0140, TM0141.
_meta.two_decks_one_plate: The scanner's last unresolved tier was six stations reading "2 decks, 1 plate". All six are now read and NONE was a miscount — the signature has three different causes. TM0051 Ferias, TM0057 Quirigua and TM0049 Carrera 53 are single island platforms whose one Vagon 1 is drawn in two segments with the crossing between them, services on both long edges; they need no layout, the bar already describes them. TM0116 Biblioteca and TM0117 Parque are one vagon drawn once per carriageway either side of a CANO, which those two sheets label in words on a blue band — the only sheets in the set that name their own divider. TM0035 Suba - Calle 100 is the odd one: its second deck carries a RED plate reading "Vagon 2 / NO OPERATIVO", a vagon that physically exists and is out of service, so the sheet prints two decks and one operating vagon on purpose. Its count of 1 is right and matches the catalog's single wagon; it is recorded here so the two decks are not "corrected" back to 2 by someone counting boxes on a later pass.
_meta.printed_what: Wagon letter -> the vagon number that wagon actually boards, read off the sheet. The counts gate is a PROXY: equal counts are taken as evidence that the letters and the plates line up in order, which is usually true. Where an entry exists here it is the answer and the counts are not consulted.
_meta.printed_why: Av. Jimenez is the case that proves the proxy can pass and still be wrong. FIVE catalog wagons, FIVE printed vagones, and the mapping is not one-to-one: wagon A is Vagon 1, D is Vagon 4 and E is Vagon 5, but B and C each carry half of Vagon 2 and half of Vagon 3, split by DIRECTION rather than by platform — C holds everything northbound across both vagones, B everything southbound. Counting alone would print "Vagon 2" for a wagon whose riders are standing at Vagon 3 half the time, and the counts would have agreed. B and C are therefore left out and take no number, while A, D and E are numbered from the sheet.
_meta.the_five_missing_sheets: The five stations whose planos never resolved from the maps API were supplied by the maintainer on 2026-09-01, and they close the two cases this dataset had written off as unreconcilable. RICAURTE and AV. JIMENEZ are each published as TWO sheets, one per troncal, joined by a pedestrian tunnel — which is exactly why no single sheet could ever match the catalog and why both were recorded as "no sheet can reconcile this". RICAURTE: sheet E (NQS Central, diciembre 2025) prints Vagon 3, 2, 1 and sheet F (Americas, agosto 2026) prints Vagon 4, 5, 6, six vagones against six catalog wagons, and the match is exact service for service — C is Vagon 3, B is Vagon 2, A is Vagon 1, D is Vagon 4, E is Vagon 5, F is Vagon 6. Its stored count goes 3 -> 6 and it is numbered for the first time. Sheet E prints G43 and G48 where the catalog files S43 and S48, both running to San Mateo: the same Soacha re-lettering seen at El Tiempo, Salitre El Greco, Modelia and Tygua. AV. JIMENEZ: sheet A (Estacion temporal, Caracas, enero 2026) prints Vagon 3, 2, 1 and sheet F (Americas, enero 2026) prints Vagon 4 and 5, five against five — but see printed_why, the mapping is not one-to-one. Its sheet F also marks the pedestrian tunnel to the Caracas half CIERRE (closed), so the two halves are not walkable between. TIBANICA - PRIMAVERA, LOS LAURELES and ISLANDIA each print two vagones and each CONFIRMS the count and the A->1 B->2 mapping already on file: at Tibanica wagon A is Vagon 1 (Z61 north, F63 south) and B is Vagon 2 (Z63 north, A61 south), while at Laureles and Islandia both Z services sit on Vagon 2 and F63 with A61 on Vagon 1. Nothing changed for those three; they are recorded because "confirmed by the sheet" and "never checked" are not the same state.
_meta.ricaurte_jimenez_no_layout_yet: Ricaurte and Av. Jimenez are NUMBERED from their sheets but not yet DRAWN, and the reason is the axis. Every layout on file is two platforms of ONE corridor, so the drawing names that corridor once along each long edge. These two are not that: each is two platform complexes on DIFFERENT troncals joined by a pedestrian tunnel. Ricaurte vagones 1-3 face AutoNorte/Suba/Calle 80/NQS Central against Caracas Sur/Carrera 10/NQS Sur, while vagones 4-6 face Americas/AV. Ciudad de Cali against Suba/Caracas/Carrera 7/Eje Ambiental. One shared axis pair would label half of each station with the other half's directions. Drawing them needs a per-row axis, which is a renderer change, not a data one. The full readings are in the_five_missing_sheets so no re-reading is needed when that lands. Note also for whoever does it: Av. Jimenez sheet F marks its tunnel to the Caracas half CIERRE (closed), so the two halves are NOT walkable between and a drawing must not imply they are.
_meta.rows_wagones: A layout row may name the catalog wagons it IS. Only the two stations the catalog files as one stop while the map resolves them as two need it — Ricaurte (NQS = A,B,C; Calle 13 = D,E,F) and Av. Jimenez (Caracas = A,B,C; Calle 13 = D,E), matching the verified splits in stationCatalogResolver. A popup opened on one platform then draws only that platform. Knowing which codigos resolve is NOT enough to decide it: route 5 terminates at Av. Jimenez, the catalog files it under a Caracas wagon, and the Calle 13 sheet also prints it on Vagon 5, so the Caracas half drew a stray Vagon 5 belonging to the platform across the tunnel. The estacion page holds every wagon of the stop and so still shows both halves, each under its own troncal label.
_meta.detalle_what: The station as its plano de ubicacion actually draws it: not only the platforms and their services, but the furniture around them — vestibules, torniquetes, taquillas, salidas with the street they come out on, pedestrian bridges, ramps and stairs. Used ONLY by the estacion page. The popup keeps the compact drawing, because a popup is a glance and a page is the thing you study before you travel.
_meta.detalle_why: Because the furniture answers questions the platforms cannot. Guatoque is the case that makes it plain: a cano separates its two platforms, and drawing only the platforms and the cano tells a rider there is no way across. There is — the sheet draws the cano starting AFTER a vestibule that spans both rows, and that vestibule, with its torniquetes and its Carrera 27 exit, is exactly how you get from Vagon 4 to Vagon 2. Leaving it out did not simplify the drawing, it made it say something false.
_meta.detalle_shape: A drawing is a sequence of COLUMNS, left to right as the sheet draws them, not two independent rows: only columns can express a vestibule that spans both platforms while the cano between them does not. Column kinds: "vestibulo" (a full-height access block, carrying salidas and icons per fila), "vagones" (a platform column, naming the vagon ABOVE and the one BELOW), "paso" (the crossing between adjacent vagones), "puente" (a pedestrian bridge). A vagones column names its vagones by NUMBER and the services come from `layouts` — the services are stated once, in one place, so the two drawings cannot drift apart.

TM0016.source: Plano de ubicación, Estación Calle 85 - GATO DUMAS, versión febrero de 2025.
TM0016.why: One straight platform of FOUR vagones; the catalog files three wagons and its C merges printed vagones 3 and 4. The stored plate count was 3, which matched the three wagons, so the gate passed and C was published as "Vagón 3" — sending anyone boarding C50, D10 or H27 to a platform they do not board. The ends are direction-specific here (Vagón 4 southbound only, Vagón 3 northbound only) while Vagón 2 and Vagón 1 serve both, which is why sides are given per vagón rather than per platform.

TM0059.source: Plano de ubicación, Estación La Castellana, versión diciembre de 2025.
TM0059.why: A staggered station: two platforms on opposite carriageways, offset from each other, with the busway between them — not one segmented bar. The catalog cannot describe it. Its two wagons each straddle BOTH platforms (A = B28 upper + G12 lower; B = B12/B72 upper + F28/H72 lower), so lettering them 1 and 2 puts services from opposite sides of the road on one platform. Printed vagones given directly instead.

TM0019.source: Plano de ubicacion, Estacion Calle 106, version junio de 2026.
TM0019.why: Four vagones on one line, but the platform is cut in half by two puente peatonal bays: Vagon 4 and Vagon 3 board only southbound (chips below), Vagon 2 and Vagon 1 only northbound (chips above). The catalog files TWO wagons and neither is a half of the platform — each pairs one southbound vagon with the northbound one across the bridge. A holds Vagon 3 (8, D55, H13) plus Vagon 1 (B11, B28); B holds Vagon 4 (F28, G11) plus Vagon 2 (8, B13, B55). Drawn from those letters it would put services from opposite ends of a split platform on one plate.

TM0026.source: Plano de ubicacion, Estacion Mazuren, version julio de 2026.
TM0026.why: Five vagones on one line against three catalog wagons. C is Vagon 5 exactly (H13, H72), but A merges Vagon 2 (8, B10, B16) with Vagon 1 (D10, K16) and B merges Vagon 3 (B13, B72, B74) with Vagon 4 (8, J70, J74) — so two of the three letters name two platforms each. Sides do not follow the halves either: Vagon 1 boards below while its neighbour Vagon 2 boards above.

TM0024.source: Plano de ubicacion, Estacion Calle 142, version noviembre de 2024.
TM0024.why: Four vagones on one line, split by the puente peatonal: Vagon 4 and Vagon 3 board southbound, Vagon 2 and Vagon 1 northbound. The catalog files TWO wagons and each pairs a vagon with the one across the bridge — A is Vagon 3 (8, C50, D55, H13, J70, J74) plus Vagon 1 (B12, B75); B is Vagon 2 (8, B13, B50, B55, B74) plus Vagon 4 (G12, H75). Both decompose exactly, so the sheet can be drawn. Same shape as Calle 106 and Calle 161.

TM0131.source: Plano de ubicacion, Estacion El Tiempo - Camara de Comercio de Bta, version febrero de 2025.
TM0131.why: Four vagones across two platforms either side of the busway — Vagon 2 and Vagon 1 on the Calle 26 side, Vagon 4 and Vagon 3 on the AutoNorte side — against TWO catalog wagons, each of which merges an upper vagon with a lower one. A holds Vagon 1 (K16, K23, K43) plus Vagon 3 (1, H54); B holds Vagon 2 (1, K54) plus Vagon 4 (B16, B23). K86 and M86 sit in wagon 0 and the sheet places them, on Vagon 2 and Vagon 3. The sheet prints G43 where the catalog now files S43: same service, re-lettered to the Soacha corridor in September 2026, after this sheet was drawn.

TM0147.source: Plano de ubicacion, Estacion Guatoque - Veraguas, version noviembre de 2024.
TM0147.why: Four vagones across two platforms either side of the cano, stored as 5. Vagon 4 and Vagon 3 above, Vagon 2 and Vagon 1 below, aligned rather than staggered. The catalog two wagons each merge one upper vagon with one lower: B is Vagon 4 (D21, S41, G47) plus Vagon 2 (8, H17, L25); A is Vagon 3 (8, C17, C25) plus Vagon 1 (H21, L41, M47). The sheet prints G41 where the catalog now files S41 — same service, re-lettered to Soacha in September 2026.

TM0129.source: Plano de ubicacion, Estacion CAN - British Council, version noviembre de 2025.
TM0129.why: Four vagones across two platforms either side of the ciclorruta — Vagon 2 and Vagon 1 on the Calle 26 / Avenida 68 side, Vagon 4 and Vagon 3 on the AutoNorte side — against TWO catalog wagons, each of which merges an upper vagon with a lower one. The sheet does not draw K53 or G53: both reached the station after November 2025, and they are listed under the drawing rather than placed on it.

TM0128.source: Plano de ubicacion, Estacion Gobernacion, version noviembre de 2024.
TM0128.why: Four vagones across two platforms either side of the ciclorruta — Vagon 2 and Vagon 1 on the Calle 26 side, Vagon 4 and Vagon 3 on the AutoNorte side — against TWO catalog wagons. This sheet is a year older than CAN next door and has drifted: it draws B16 on Vagon 4, and the catalog files B23 here and no B16 at all. B16 is NOT recorded as B23 — that would be guessing a successor — it is simply not drawn, because drawing a service the station does not run is the one disagreement that invalidates a sheet. B23 and S43 (the September 2026 Soacha re-lettering of G43, which postdates the sheet) are listed under the drawing instead. Re-read this plano when a newer version is published.

TM0060.source: Plano de ubicacion, Estacion Calle 75 - Zona M, version noviembre de 2024.
TM0060.why: TWO vagones, each drawn once per carriageway, either side of the railway that runs down the NQS. Both rows read "Vagon 2, Vagon 1" — this is not four vagones like Gobernacion, it is two with a face on each side of the tracks. The catalog agrees exactly: wagon A is the printed Vagon 1 (B12, E32 north; 4 to Portal Sur, F32, L25 south) and wagon B is the printed Vagon 2 (4 to Heroes, C25, D22 north; G12, G22 south), so the count is 2 and A->1, B->2 holds. Stored count corrected from 4, which had counted the four drawn bars instead of the two vagones they name.

TM0061.source: Plano de ubicacion, Estacion Av. Chile, version noviembre de 2024.
TM0061.why: THREE vagones, each drawn once per carriageway, either side of the railway down the NQS — six bars naming three vagones, both rows reading "Vagon 3, Vagon 2, Vagon 1". The catalog maps onto them exactly: wagon A is Vagon 1 (4 to Heroes, B72 north; 4 to Portal Sur, H72 south), wagon B is Vagon 2 (B16, C25 north; K16, L25 south), wagon C is Vagon 3 (D22, E32 north; F32, G22 south). Count 3 already on file and already equal to the wagon count, so this adds the shape and the divider, not a number.

TM0130.source: Plano de ubicacion, Estacion Salitre El Greco - Vive Claro, version noviembre de 2025.
TM0130.why: Four vagones across two platforms either side of the ciclorruta, the Gobernacion/CAN shape: Vagon 2 and Vagon 1 on the Calle 26 / Avenida 68 side, Vagon 4 and Vagon 3 on the AutoNorte side, against TWO catalog wagons. Wagon B is Vagon 2 plus Vagon 4, wagon A is Vagon 1 plus Vagon 3, so no vagon number can be published. Every service the catalog files here is placed and the sheet claims nothing extra. It prints G43 where the catalog now files S43 — same service, re-lettered to the Soacha corridor in September 2026, after this sheet was drawn; the same substitution already recorded at El Tiempo. Stored count corrected from 5.

TM0134.source: Plano de ubicacion, Estacion Modelia, version noviembre de 2024.
TM0134.why: Four vagones across two platforms either side of the ciclorruta, the same shape as its Calle 26 neighbours: Vagon 2 and Vagon 1 on the Calle 26 side, Vagon 4 and Vagon 3 on the AutoNorte side, against TWO catalog wagons — B is Vagon 2 plus Vagon 4, A is Vagon 1 plus Vagon 3. Every catalog service is placed and nothing extra is drawn. G43 is recorded as S43, the September 2026 Soacha re-lettering, as at El Tiempo and Salitre El Greco. Stored count corrected from 5.

TM0148.source: Plano de ubicacion, Estacion Tygua - San Jose, version noviembre de 2024.
TM0148.why: TWO vagones, each drawn once per carriageway either side of the ciclorruta — both rows read "Vagon 2, Vagon 1". The catalog maps onto them exactly: wagon A is the printed Vagon 1 (B72, S41, G47 on the AutoNorte side; M47, L41 on the other) and wagon B is Vagon 2 (8 to Terminal, C25; 8 to Guatoque, H72, L25), so the count is 2 and A->1, B->2 holds. Stored count corrected from 4, which counted the four drawn bars rather than the two vagones they name. The sheet prints G41 where the catalog now files S41: that route ends at San Mateo, a Soacha station, and the September 2026 re-lettering moved exactly those services to the S letter — which is also why G47 beside it keeps its G, since it stops at Portal Sur.

TM0030.source: Plano de ubicacion, Estacion Calle 187, version noviembre de 2024.
TM0030.why: ONE vagon, drawn once per carriageway — both decks read "Vagon 1" and the sheet prints no second plate anywhere. The catalog files TWO wagons here and both of them carry services in BOTH directions, so its A/B grouping is not the platform split and cannot be reconciled with a single printed vagon; this is the Calle 161 / Av. Jimenez case, and the numbering gate stays shut on it (1 plate against 2 wagons). Stored count corrected from 3. What the sheet does settle is the shape, and the catalog agrees with it independently: the chips drawn above the top deck are exactly the services the direction plan calls norte (8 to Terminal, B11, B16, B18) and those below the bottom deck are exactly the sur ones (8 to Guatoque, G11, K16, L18). B55 and D55 are in the catalog but not on this sheet; they list under the drawing. The DIVIDER is a green median, and it is the one on file with the weakest provenance. The sheet draws no band between the decks at all, only a blank callout box. It was answered from satellite imagery supplied by the maintainer, which shows the two platforms separated by a wide landscaped strip of grass and mature trees, with the Autopista Norte carriageways OUTSIDE both of them — which is also why the sheet puts chips only on the outer edge of each deck. The maintainer has explicitly NOT been to this station, so unlike every other divider here this one is read off a picture rather than answered by someone who has stood there. Treat it as the weakest claim in the set.

TM0116.source: Plano de ubicacion, Estacion Biblioteca, version noviembre de 2024.
TM0116.why: ONE vagon, drawn once per carriageway either side of a CANO — and this sheet does not leave it to be guessed, it prints the word "Cano" on the blue band between the two decks. Both decks read "Vagon 1", the catalog files one wagon, and the two agree, so the station is numbered. Biblioteca boards B13 to Portal Norte on the AutoNorte side and H13 to Portal Tunal on the Caracas Sur side. Stored count corrected from 2, which had counted the two drawn decks rather than the one vagon they both name.

TM0117.source: Plano de ubicacion, Estacion Parque, version noviembre de 2024.
TM0117.why: ONE vagon, drawn once per carriageway either side of a CANO — and this sheet does not leave it to be guessed, it prints the word "Cano" on the blue band between the two decks. Both decks read "Vagon 1", the catalog files one wagon, and the two agree, so the station is numbered. Parque boards C15 to Portal Suba on the Suba side and H15 to Portal Tunal on the Caracas Sur side. Stored count corrected from 2, which had counted the two drawn decks rather than the one vagon they both name.

TM0132.source: Plano de ubicacion, Estacion AV. Rojas - UNISALESIANA, version noviembre de 2024.
TM0132.why: SIX vagones across two platforms either side of the ciclorruta — Vagon 3, 2, 1 on the Calle 26 side and Vagon 6, 5, 4 on the AutoNorte side — against THREE catalog wagons that each merge one upper vagon with one lower: A is Vagon 1 (K16, K23) plus Vagon 4 (B16, B23), B is Vagon 2 (1, K54) plus Vagon 5 (1, H54), and K86 and M86 sit in wagon 0 while the sheet places them on Vagon 3 and Vagon 6. Numbering stays withheld, as it must: publishing A as "Vagon 1" sent half its riders across the ciclorruta.
TM0132.filed_late: This layout was withheld until 2026-09-01 for a reason that no longer holds. The sheet predates G53 and K53, and the layout gate used to DROP any layout that failed to draw a service the station runs — so filing it would have deleted both from the page. The gate now treats a missing service as what it is, a sheet older than the network, and the client lists every service a drawing does not place. G53 and K53 appear under the drawing.

TM0069.source: Dos planos: "E | Estacion Ricaurte" (NQS Central, diciembre 2025) y "F | Estacion Ricaurte" (Americas, agosto 2026).
TM0069.why: Ricaurte is TWO stations the catalog files as one. Sheet E prints Vagon 3, 2, 1 on the NQS Central platform; sheet F prints Vagon 4, 5, 6 on the Americas platform; they are joined by a pedestrian tunnel and by nothing else. Drawing them merged, sharing one pair of direction labels, told half the station the other half's directions — vagones 1-3 face AutoNorte/Suba/Calle 80/NQS Central against Caracas Sur/Carrera 10/NQS Sur, while vagones 4-6 face Americas/AV. Ciudad de Cali against Suba/Caracas/Carrera 7/Eje Ambiental. Each row now names its own troncal. The six vagones map one-to-one onto the six catalog wagons, service for service and edge for edge, and the direction plan agrees independently on every one. Sheet E prints G43 and G48 where the catalog files S43 and S48, both to San Mateo — the Soacha re-lettering.

TM0013.source: Dos planos: "A | Estacion temporal Av. Jimenez" (Caracas, enero 2026) y "F | Estacion Av. Jimenez" (Americas, enero 2026).
TM0013.why: Av. Jimenez is TWO stations the catalog files as one, and its halves do NOT carry the same services: the Caracas half (Vagon 3, 2, 1) and the Americas half (Vagon 4, 5) share only route 5, which terminates here. Each row names its own troncal for that reason. THE DIVIDER IS DELIBERATELY UNNAMED. There is a pedestrian tunnel between the halves and sheet F strikes it through in red, CIERRE, closed — so it is not drawn. Naming a crossing nobody can use is worse than naming nothing, and the maintainer settled it: no reason to display something people cannot cross. Ricaurte, whose tunnel is open, does get the label. On the numbering see printed_why: wagons B and C each straddle Vagon 2 and Vagon 3 split by direction, C northbound and B southbound, so only A, D and E take a number. Route 5 is drawn on BOTH halves because both sheets print it — it arrives along Americas and terminates on the Caracas platform.

TM0147.source: Plano de ubicacion, Estacion Guatoque - Veraguas, version noviembre de 2024.
TM0147.why: Read off the vestibule column at 3x, which settled placements two earlier passes got wrong. The taquilla is in the UPPER band beside the Carrera 27 exit, the TORNIQUETES are in the MIDDLE band — level with the cano, which is what a rider crosses there — and a second taquilla is in the LOWER band. The ramp arrows and the emergency figure are NOT in the vestibule at all: they sit in a narrow grey channel between it and Vagon 4, the same channel the sheet draws between Vagon 4 and Vagon 3. The cano crosses that second channel and stops short of the first.

TM0061.source: Plano de ubicacion, Estacion Av. Chile, version noviembre de 2024.
TM0061.why: Read off the sheet at both ends. A puente peatonal at each, drawn full height because it crosses the road the station sits in. Inside each bridge an access block: taquilla in the upper band, torniquetes in the middle where a rider crosses the railway, and the street exit below — Calle 72 west, Calle 70 east. The right-hand block is MIRRORED: its equipment and its way through sit on its LEFT, because that is the end nearest the platform, and its exit arrow points out to the right. The ramp arrows and the walking figure are not tiles in the block; they are the channel at its platform edge. The three vagones are drawn once per carriageway either side of the railway, so both rows read 3, 2, 1.
